nodes.text: Terrace kitchen! Miners eat first, smiths second, travelers wherever there's a bench-end going spare. You look like a bench-end sort. Sit — the stew's at the good stage.

choices.text: Two hundred hands off two hearths — how?
What's the terrace saying these days?

nodes.text: Volume, timing, and fear. The stew never stops — it's the same pot my predecessor lit, topped and tended, older than half the miners eating from it. The bread runs on Ivo's wheat and the trout on the gate mongers, and the whole machine turns on everyone being too well-fed to argue with me. Armies march on their stomachs. My terrace *sprints*.

Deep talk, all of it. Who's transferred below, what the ore broker's paying, whether the digmaster's tunnel truly points at the starfall — and every third bowl, somebody's heard the spider's web creak personally. The mountain gossips upward, traveler. It all reaches my benches eventually, salted.
Stew, bread, roast, and pool trout done proper. Eat it while it's arguing.
